hypothesis: Adding structured, RCA-oriented instrumentation (LLM interaction event schema, OpenTelemetry traces/logs, and explicit feedback/guardrail signals) to an LLM gateway produces high-fidelity, query-correlatable RCA signals without materially impacting p95 latency (≤10% overhead) or causing sensitive prompt/PII leakage in stored events.

baseline.description: Minimal LLM gateway without RCA-oriented instrumentation. Logs only coarse request metrics (timestamp, HTTP status, total latency) and opaque JSON request/response bodies with no standardized schema, tracing, or explicit RCA signals.

components: Python FastAPI (or similar) LLM gateway exposing POST /v1/chat/completions
LLM client using environment-configured provider (e.g., OpenAI-compatible API or local model wrapper)
Naive logging using standard Python logging to stdout or a local file without structured fields
key_characteristics: No request/trace IDs beyond default web framework logs
No standardized LLM interaction event schema
No explicit recording of user feedback, guardrail triggers, or evaluator scores

treatment.description: RCA-instrumented LLM gateway that emits structured LLM interaction events, OpenTelemetry traces/logs, and explicit RCA signals (feedback, guardrails, evaluator scores) into a minimal observability pipeline.
instrumentation_features: Canonical LLM interaction event schema with request, response, routing, and context metadata
Stable correlation IDs across HTTP request, LLM call, and downstream tools (trace_id, span_id, interaction_id)
OpenTelemetry tracing with spans for HTTP request, LLM invocation, guardrail evaluation, and feedback recording
Structured logs (JSON) for each interaction event and sub-event using the common schema
Explicit RCA signals: user_feedback, guardrail_triggered, evaluator_score, failure_category
Configurable redaction and hashing for sensitive fields (raw prompts, user identifiers, tool arguments)
privacy_and_safety_measures: Redaction of raw user text by default, with optional safe sampling for non-prod
Configurable allowlist/denylist of logged fields via YAML config
Environment toggle to fully disable content capture in production environments

components: Instrumented FastAPI gateway app with OpenTelemetry middleware and manual spans
Event schema definition as Python dataclasses and JSON Schema
OpenTelemetry SDK initialization (OTLP exporter to local collector)
Local OpenTelemetry Collector configuration exporting traces/logs to stdout or file
Feedback endpoint to simulate and capture user feedback events
Simple guardrail function (e.g., regex-based or heuristic) emitting guardrail spans and events
Optional offline evaluator script scoring responses (synthetic quality/safety scores)

workloads.name: synthetic-mixed-traffic
workloads.description: Synthetic mixed workload simulating diverse LLM usage patterns (short Q&A, RAG-like queries with metadata, multi-turn chat, and tool-like calls) with injected edge cases and failures to validate instrumentation coverage and data quality.

request_mix.example: What is the capital of France?
According to the internal policy corpus, what is our PTO policy?
Help me draft an email to my manager about project delays.

patterns.name: guardrail_violation
patterns.behavior: Inject prompts with banned phrases to trigger guardrail rules and record guardrail_triggered=true events.

patterns.name: llm_timeout
patterns.behavior: Artificially sleep beyond timeout threshold before returning or raising a timeout exception.

patterns.name: routing_error
patterns.behavior: Route some requests to a deliberately slow or error-prone mock model.

feedback_and_evaluation.user_feedback_model: Synthetic labeling based on prompt/response heuristics (e.g., reward simple factual correctness, penalize gibberish or guardrail hits).

environmental_controls: Run baseline and treatment in identical container images except for instrumentation-specific dependencies.
Pin Python version (e.g., 3.11.x) and all Python dependencies via requirements.txt/poetry.lock.
Use the same LLM backend configuration (same model name, temperature, max_tokens, and provider) between baseline and treatment.
Run on the same host type (e.g., 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM) or the same Kubernetes node pool.
Disable non-experiment background workloads on the host to reduce interference.
experimental_design: Run synthetic-mixed-traffic against baseline first, then treatment, then repeat in reverse order (treatment then baseline) to check for drift.
Use deterministic random seeds for workload generation (e.g., --seed 42) so that baseline and treatment see identical request sequences.
Maintain identical workload parameters (duration, RPS, concurrency, failure injection config) across baseline and treatment runs.
Store raw telemetry outputs from baseline and treatment in separate, clearly named directories for later comparison.
privacy_controls: Set instrumentation configuration to redact or hash any field labeled as potentially sensitive in the schema configuration file (e.g., config/instrumentation.yaml).
Ensure synthetic workload only uses non-PII prompts; when templates include names, use randomly generated or obviously synthetic entities.
Disable full prompt/response capture in production-like environment by default; enable only for local testing via environment flag (e.g., LLM_RCA_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true).

performance: Relative increase in gateway_p95_latency_ms between baseline and treatment is ≤ 10%.
instrumentation_overhead_ms_per_request ≤ 15 ms on average under synthetic-mixed-traffic workload.
data_quality: trace_coverage_fraction ≥ 0.98 for all successful HTTP requests.
event_linkage_rate ≥ 0.95 (LLM spans and interaction events correctly linked to HTTP request traces).
schema_compliance_rate ≥ 0.99 after JSON Schema validation of stored events.
rca_signal_coverage: feedback_signal_coverage ≥ 0.9 for workloads where synthetic feedback is configured.
guardrail_trigger_capture_rate ≥ 0.98 for requests that hit the guardrail in application logic.
privacy_and_safety: No raw prompts or user identifiers appear in stored telemetry when content capture is disabled by configuration.
operational_robustness: No increase > 5% in gateway_error_rate attributable to instrumentation (e.g., exceptions in instrumentation code).

failure_modes.name: high_latency_overhead
failure_modes.description: Instrumentation adds excessive processing delay, causing p95 latency to regress beyond acceptable thresholds.

failure_modes.name: partial_or_inconsistent_tracing
failure_modes.description: Not all HTTP requests produce root traces, or LLM spans are not reliably attached to the correct parent spans.

failure_modes.name: schema_drift_or_validation_failures
failure_modes.description: Emitted events frequently fail schema validation, making downstream analysis brittle or unreliable.

failure_modes.name: privacy_leakage
failure_modes.description: Sensitive data (raw user prompts, PII, internal URLs) are present in stored events despite redaction configuration.

failure_modes.name: excessive_log_volume
failure_modes.description: Events and traces are too verbose, producing unsustainable log volume per request and potential storage/backpressure issues.

failure_modes.name: instrumentation-induced_errors
failure_modes.description: Application returns 5xx errors or crashes due to instrumentation (e.g., exporter failures, serialization errors).

failure_modes.name: missing_rca_signals
failure_modes.description: Guardrail triggers, feedback scores, or evaluator outputs are not consistently captured and linked to the originating interaction.

services.name: llm_backend
services.description: LLM provider API or local model endpoint. For reproducibility, use an OpenAI-compatible mock server provided in the repo or a small local model.

services.name: opentelemetry_collector
services.description: Local OpenTelemetry Collector instance receiving OTLP traces and logs from the instrumented gateway.

optional_orchestration.kubernetes: Optional, for readers who wish to run gateway and collector as pods.

run_instructions:
1. Clone the companion repository:
   git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/automated-rca-llm-failures
   cd automated-rca-llm-failures

2. Create and activate a Python virtual environment (example using venv):
   python3.11 -m venv .venv
   source .venv/bin/activate

4. Configure LLM backend for reproducible runs:
   - For local/mock backend, follow instructions in README under gateway/ or mock_llm/ to start the mock LLM server.
   - Set environment variables, for example:
     export LLM_API_BASE="http://localhost:8001/v1"
     export LLM_API_KEY="test-key"
     export LLM_MODEL_NAME="mock-llm-v1"

5. Start the OpenTelemetry Collector using the provided configuration:
   otelcol --config otel/collector-config.yaml
   # Or, if using Docker:
   docker compose -f otel/docker-compose.yaml up

6. Run the BASELINE gateway (non-instrumented):
   export LLM_RCA_INSTRUMENTATION_ENABLED="false"
   uvicorn gateway.baseline_app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --log-level info

7. In a separate terminal, run the synthetic workload against the baseline:
   source .venv/bin/activate
   python workloads/synthetic_workload.py \
       --api-base http://localhost:8000 \
       --duration-seconds 600 \
       --concurrency 5 \
       --target-rps 5 \
       --seed 42 \
       --output-dir runs/baseline
   # This script should record basic HTTP metrics (latency, errors) and store them in runs/baseline/metrics.json.
8. Stop the baseline gateway process after the workload completes.

9. Run the TREATMENT gateway (instrumented):
   export LLM_RCA_INSTRUMENTATION_ENABLED="true"
   export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="http://localhost:4317"
   export LLM_RCA_REDACTION_CONFIG="config/instrumentation.yaml"
   uvicorn gateway.instrumented_app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --log-level info

10. In a separate terminal, re-run the same synthetic workload against the treatment:
    source .venv/bin/activate
    python workloads/synthetic_workload.py \
        --api-base http://localhost:8000 \
        --duration-seconds 600 \
        --concurrency 5 \
        --target-rps 5 \
        --seed 42 \
        --output-dir runs/treatment
    # This script, when instrumentation is enabled, should additionally trigger feedback and evaluator calls
    # and may provide simple summaries of observed guardrail hits and evaluator scores.
11. (Optional) Repeat runs in reverse order (treatment first, then baseline) to check for environmental drift, using a different output directory suffix (e.g., runs/baseline_2, runs/treatment_2).

12. Validate telemetry and instrumentation quality using the analysis script:
    python analysis/check_instrumentation_quality.py \
        --baseline-run runs/baseline \
        --treatment-run runs/treatment \
        --otel-logs-dir otel/output \
        --schema-file config/llm_interaction_schema.json \
        --report-file runs/summary_report.json

13. Inspect the generated summary report and raw telemetry:
    - runs/summary_report.json: high-level comparison of metrics and success criteria.
    - otel/output/: raw traces/logs exported by the collector for manual inspection.
    - runs/*/events.jsonl (if produced): raw structured LLM interaction events for schema validation and spot checks.

14. Manually verify privacy redaction:
    - Grep for sample sensitive tokens from the synthetic workload (e.g., specific user names or emails) in otel/output and runs/*/events.jsonl.
    - Confirm that, when redaction is enabled in config/instrumentation.yaml, these tokens do not appear in stored events.

15. Archive experiment artifacts for reproducibility:
    - Tar or zip the runs/ directory, otel/output/, and relevant config files.
    - Record Git commit hash and environment details (python --version, pip freeze) in a README within the run artifact directory.

baseline_metrics.description: Aggregated HTTP-level metrics for baseline runs.

treatment_metrics.description: Aggregated HTTP-level metrics for treatment runs, plus instrumentation-specific metrics if computed.

llm_interaction_events.description: Line-delimited JSON records of LLM interaction events captured by the instrumented gateway.

otel_traces_and_logs.description: Raw OpenTelemetry export logs and traces as collected by the local collector.

instrumentation_quality_report.description: Computed metrics and pass/fail status against success criteria for this experiment.
